solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: G7 finally release statement after 30 days

indicators.note: after places the closing letters behind the month

parts.note: September has thirty days, abbreviated to Sept

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A summit communiqué from the G7 nations is due out a month on.
explanation.walkthrough: G7 looks like the group of nations, but here it is simply a group of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven, such as seven musicians, is called a septet.

clue.text: Unreliable, like a mule?

definitions.meaning: a mule is a backless slipper, so something resembling one is jokingly slipper-y

explanation.walkthrough: A mule is a kind of backless shoe, not only the animal; the second reading adds -Y to the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifty person is described as slippery; the question mark flags the punning footwear sense.

clue.text: Exotic posh panties — or bloomers?

indicators.note: exotic suggests something foreign and strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence posh
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fancy lingerie described as an alternative to old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are baggy underwear in the surface, but here they are flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Petunias are garden plants grown for their flowers, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Pilgrim uplifted and overcome by last third of Handel oratorio

indicators.note: overcome by means sitting beneath, so in this down entry the reversed pilgrim comes below
the last third of a six-letter word is its final two letters
uplifted in a down clue means the word for pilgrim is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A pilgrim is moved and overwhelmed by the closing part of a Handel oratorio.
explanation.walkthrough: Handel only supplies letters; the surface makes it look like the composer of the oratorio, which is actually by Mendelssohn.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is a famous oratorio by Mendelssohn, a large choral work on the prophet's life.

clue.text: Setter's really rude

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so setter's is I am, shortened to I'm
proper as an intensifier, as in a proper mess, means really

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler admits to being genuinely offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper remarks are indecent or rude, breaking the rules of good taste.

clue.text: Second husband to publish yarn

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second, as in wait a mo
to air something is to make it public

explanation.surface: A remarried woman's new husband wants to broadcast a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarn looks like a tall tale, but it is the knitting wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a yarn spun from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Repeatedly copy screech of bear

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the words screech of carry the entry inside them

explanation.surface: A bear lets out a screech that is echoed over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-echo is to echo again and again, copying a sound repeatedly.

clue.text: Tragic air of quiet musketeer

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: A silent musketeer has a mournful look about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses pity or sadness, a tragic atmosphere.

clue.text: Offensive clues regularly get up your nose

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling or offensive

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word clues

explanation.surface: Insulting crossword clues are bound to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up your nose' is British slang for to irritate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles causes lasting irritation, just as an annoyance gets up your nose.

clue.text: Over time northern folk work things out instinctively

indicators.note: over means covering, so the people's name lies over and around the abbreviation for time

parts.note: the Inuit are a people of the Arctic north

explanation.surface: In time, people of the far north solve problems by gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to understand by instinct rather than reasoning.

clue.text: Leader of Taliban in Teheran cast as menace

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters of the city are rearranged

explanation.surface: The head of the Taliban, in the Iranian capital, is portrayed as a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: God unhappy about endangered animals

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for unhappy is read backwards

parts.note: unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: A deity is upset about creatures facing extinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant pandas are a well-known example of a species at risk of dying out.

clue.text: Riddle of early human is about to be raised

indicators.note: about means turned round and raised means lifted up in a down clue, so the two words are read upwards

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the first woman, whose fame is set to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddle looks like a puzzle, but it is a coarse sieve, also used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel.

clue.text: Light now breaking, he may go to bed at last

definitions.text: he may go to bed at last

indicators.note: breaking means shattering the words so their letters reform

explanation.surface: Dawn light is breaking, and a late-night reveller finally heads to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who stays up late and only goes to bed in the small hours.

clue.text: One wept boundlessly over melody, part of Planets Suite

indicators.note: over places the first pieces above the next in this down entry
boundlessly removes the outer letters from each of the two words

parts.note: a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Someone weeps uncontrollably over a tune from a famous orchestral suite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Planets is Holst's orchestral suite; its last movement is Neptune, the Mystic.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the final movement of Holst's suite The Planets.

clue.text: Pedestrian former president taking part in "60 Minutes"

indicators.note: taking part in means going inside, so the president sits within the hour abbreviation

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour, abbreviated hr
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: An ex-president appears on a TV news show and is found rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Pedestrian looks like an adjective meaning dull, but here it is a noun: someone on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker on foot, such as a rambler, is a pedestrian.

clue.text: Reagan as his friends knew him — astride a horse

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the name sits on either side of the letter

parts.words: Reagan as his friends knew him
parts.note: Ronald Reagan was called Ron by friends

explanation.surface: The president, known informally to friends, sits on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat is mixed with white hairs.

clue.text: Attempt to frighten gutless scaredy-cat in lift

parts.note: boo is what you shout to frighten someone

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Trying to scare a cowardly cat while riding in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift looks like the British word for an elevator, but it means a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a lift is to raise or encourage, the same sense as a boost.

clue.text: Pub eschewing break with tradition? Cheers!

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the pub is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: innovation is a new departure from established ways
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub abandons custom by doing away with something, and the regulars applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause and cheering from an audience.

clue.text: In embrace of courtesan it is easy to block out unpleasant things

indicators.note: in the embrace of means held inside, so the entry sits within the words

explanation.surface: In the arms of a courtesan it is easy to forget life's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise is to remove what is unpleasant or offensive, making things seem acceptable.

clue.text: Get individual rubbed out, source of adrenaline perhaps in underworld

indicators.note: rubbed out means erased, so the letter for the individual is removed

parts.note: to gain is to get
I is a single individual, a crossword convention
the adrenal gland is one example of a gland producing adrenaline

explanation.surface: A gangster has someone killed, getting a rush of adrenaline in the criminal world.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland is the world of organised crime, the criminal underworld.

clue.text: Slightly contrary information

indicators.note: contrary means running the opposite way, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a tad means slightly or a little

explanation.surface: A bit of conflicting intelligence comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, a body of information.

clue.text: Deep rifts originally announced via text message

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: by means via, as in travel by Paris
SMS is short message service, a text

explanation.surface: Deep divisions were first revealed by text message.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysms are archaic forms of abysses, deep chasms or rifts.

clue.text: In heaven at first, engrossed in a book

indicators.note: engrossed in means absorbed into, so the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of heaven

explanation.surface: Lost in a good book, a reader is in seventh heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is the definition: being in is being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in, not out, is at home in their house.

clue.text: Banks could be retrieving reputation in US, I'm afraid

indicators.note: retrieving suggests bringing back, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: rep is American slang for reputation
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Banks may be trying to recover their reputation in America, says a frightened observer.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks looks like financial firms, but Gordon Banks was England's 1966 World Cup goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Banks was a famous goalkeeper, so he is an example of one who keeps goal.

clue.text: Told about hard grind

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for told is read backwards

parts.note: to sing is to inform, so told is sang
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone recounted the story of tough, grinding toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash the teeth is to grind them together.

clue.text: Dance wildly with judge after sex party, half-cut

indicators.note: after places the remains of the party before the word for judge
half-cut removes half of the word, here its first two letters

parts.note: an orgy is a sex party
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Someone dances wildly with a judge after a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to whirl or spin around, moving like a wild dancer.

clue.text: A pricking feeling in gut, buttock and thigh

indicators.note: pricking means piercing, so the letter goes into the word for a gut feeling

parts.note: a hunch is a gut feeling

explanation.surface: A tingling sensation in the stomach, bottom and leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The haunch is the part of the body made up of the buttock and thigh.

clue.text: See you pocketing thorium in passing

indicators.note: pocketing means holding inside, so the farewell surrounds the symbol

parts.note: bye-bye is an informal farewell like see you
Th is the chemical symbol for thorium

explanation.surface: A farewell stashes away radioactive metal while passing through.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to add a remark incidentally, meaning in passing.

clue.text: Getting money off people is hard work

explanation.definitionFit: Taxing means both imposing a levy and being burdensome or demanding.

clue.text: Not quite twenty, Joanna shortly celebrating autumn birthday

indicators.note: not quite means lacking the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: Joanna is rhyming slang for piano

explanation.surface: Joanna, nearly twenty, has a birthday party in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano. A Scorpio is born in late October or November.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under Scorpio has a birthday in late autumn.

clue.text: Unlimited suspension, a pain in the neck

indicators.note: unlimited removes the limits, the first and last letters

parts.note: hanging is suspension

explanation.surface: An indefinite ban is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain in the neck' looks like a nuisance, but angina is chest pain that can spread to the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is heart pain that often radiates to the jaw and throat.

clue.text: Drunken heiress ringing Ram's Head for wines

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the rearranged letters surround the initial
drunken means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy heiress encircles the Ram's Head pub, looking for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges HEIRESS into SHERIES, and 'ringing' puts R (the head of 'Ram's') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherries are fortified wines from southern Spain.

clue.text: Will's Kate ultimately described as "canny"

parts.note: Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; Will is Shakespeare

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Prince William's wife Kate is described as astute.
explanation.walkthrough: Will's Kate suggests Prince William's wife, but Will is Shakespeare and his Kate is the shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and canny are synonyms for astute.
